title: Saving data
objective: Store numbers, text, arrays and objects with localStorage; load saved data when the page opens and use default values
story: Does your score reset when you reload the page? At the last stop of the Event Belt we give your ship a **memory**: thanks to localStorage, information stays even after the page closes.

sections.title: localStorage: the browser's notebook
sections.body:
`localStorage` is a small notebook that every site has in the browser. Its contents stay even if the page closes or the computer restarts. Information is stored as **key** and **value** pairs:

```js
localStorage.setItem("pilot", "Ada");      // save
const name = localStorage.getItem("pilot"); // read → "Ada"
localStorage.removeItem("pilot");          // delete
localStorage.getItem("pilot");             // no record → null
```

While you experiment, you can wipe the notebook by typing `localStorage.clear()` in the Console.

sections.title: Numbers are stored as text
sections.body:
`localStorage` stores everything as **text**. If you save a number and read it back, you get text; turn it into a number with `Number(...)` before doing math:

```js
localStorage.setItem("best", 42);
localStorage.getItem("best");                           // "42" (text!)
const best = Number(localStorage.getItem("best")) || 0; // 42
```

If there's no record, `getItem` gives `null`, and `Number(null)` is `0`. The `|| 0` at the end makes sure 0 is used for values that count as false, like `NaN`.

- `a || b`: uses `b` if `a` counts as false (`0`, `""`, `null`, `NaN`...).
- `a ?? b`: uses `b` only if `a` is `null` or `undefined`. `0` and `""` are kept.

sections.title: Arrays and objects: JSON
sections.body:
To store an array or object, first turn it into **JSON** text (`JSON.stringify`) and turn it back when reading (`JSON.parse`). You remember this from Day 12:

```js
const items = ["shield", "laser"];
localStorage.setItem("inventory", JSON.stringify(items)); // '["shield","laser"]'

const back = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("inventory")) ?? [];
console.log(back.length); // 2
```

`JSON.parse(null)` gives `null`; thanks to `?? []` we use an empty array when there's no record.

sections.title: Load on open, save on change
sections.body:
Every page that saves data follows the same pattern:

1. When the page opens, **load** the saved data (use a default if there is none).
2. **Show** the data on the screen.
3. **Save** it again every time it changes.

For objects like settings, spread (`...`) helps fill missing fields with defaults:

```js
const DEFAULTS = { sound: true, volume: 5 };
const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("settings")) ?? {};
const settings = { ...DEFAULTS, ...saved }; // saved values overwrite the defaults
```

Putting the loading into a function like `loadBest()` makes things easier: you can try it again and again with different records.

tasks.title: Visit counter
tasks.prompt:
Write the `countVisit()` function:

- it reads the number in the `visits` key (0 if missing),
- adds 1 and saves it back,
- writes `You opened this page 5 times.` into `#info`.

`countVisit()` runs once when the page opens. (When the book's screenshot was taken, the notebook held 4 visits.)

tasks.title: Remember the pilot
tasks.prompt:
Write the `showGreeting()` function: if a name is saved in the `pilot` key, it writes `Welcome back, Alex!` into `#hello`; otherwise `Hello, new pilot!`. It runs when the page opens.

- When `#name-form` is submitted, the name (spaces trimmed, if not empty) is saved in the `pilot` key and the greeting is updated.
- The `#forget` button deletes the record (`removeItem`) and updates the greeting.
hints: const name = localStorage.getItem("pilot"); gives null if there's no record.

tasks.title: Saving the inventory
tasks.prompt:
The inventory is an array, stored as JSON in the `inventory` key.

- `loadItems()`: reads the record with `JSON.parse` and returns the array; returns `[]` if there's no record.
- `addItem(name)`: adds the name to the `items` array, saves the array with `JSON.stringify` and calls `render()`.

challenge.title: Remember the settings
challenge.prompt:
The game settings are stored as an object, in JSON, in the `settings` key. The defaults: `{ sound: true, volume: 5 }`.

- `loadSettings()`: reads the record and returns it with missing fields filled from the defaults (`{ ...DEFAULTS, ...saved }`). If there's no record, the defaults are returned.
- When the page opens, the `#sound` checkbox and the `#volume` list show the loaded settings.
- When either one changes (`change`), the settings object is updated and saved. `volume` is stored as a **number**.

project_task.title: High score
project_task.prompt:
The game's record should stay even after the page closes. Write two functions:

- `loadBest()`: returns the score in the `best` key as a **number** (0 if there's no record).
- `saveBest(score)`: if the score beats the record, it saves it, updates `#best`, writes `New record: 50!` into `#info` and returns `true`; otherwise it changes nothing and returns `false`.

When the page opens, the record shows in `#best`. (When the book's screenshot was taken, the record was 35.)
